name: submit_data
description: Submit the finished data definition for the widget. Call it once the pipeline has been tested with run_query and returns exactly the brief's figures. The submission is checked automatically (schema, parameters, units and formats, a live run with the sample parameters, catalog references); if anything fails you get the reasons back - fix them and submit again.

params.description: The parameters the pipeline references as {"$param": "name"}. Declare asOfDate (type date) whenever the pipeline uses it.

name.description: clientId or asOfDate (or another page parameter)

collection.description: A data collection of the bank database (see the data dictionary), e.g. holdings.

pipeline.description: MongoDB aggregation stages, read-only. Reference parameters as {"$param": "clientId"} / {"$param": "asOfDate"}; never literal client ids or dates.

columns.description: Every field each result row has, in display order.

unit.description: USD for money; ratio for a 0-1 fraction; percent for a value already 0-100; count; date; none.

format.description: Must agree with unit: USD->currency, ratio->percent, percent->percentPoints, count->integer, date->date.

measures.description: One entry per numeric column: how it is defined and where the definition comes from.

definition.description: Plain-language definition as computed by the pipeline.

catalogReference.description: collection.field or collection.derivedMetricName from the data dictionary that this figure is based on, e.g. holdings.drawnUsd or clients.utilization.

expectedShape.description: What the rows should look like, e.g. 'one row per quarter, 8 rows, ascending'.

emptyIsExpected.description: true only if an empty result is a legitimate outcome for some clients (e.g. a client with no covenants) and the sample happened to be empty.

assumptions.description: Data-level choices the banker should know about (e.g. 'counts only open deals').
